text: Business economics is best described as the application of economic theory to
subject: Business Economics I
options: Business decision making|Government budgeting|Political analysis|Social welfare
explanation: Business economics applies microeconomic analysis to the decisions of the firm.

text: The problem of what to produce how to produce and for whom to produce arises due to
subject: Business Economics I
options: Scarcity of resources|Government policy|Perfect information|Unlimited resources
explanation: Scarcity forces every economy to choose among competing uses of limited resources.

text: Opportunity cost is the value of the
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Opportunity cost measures what is sacrificed when a choice is made.

text: Microeconomics studies individual firms and households rather than the whole economy
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Microeconomics focuses on individual economic units while macroeconomics studies aggregates.

text: State the central problems of an economy
subject: Business Economics I
correctAnswer: What to produce how to produce and for whom to produce.
explanation: These three allocation problems follow from the scarcity of resources.

text: Explain the nature of business economics
subject: Business Economics I
correctAnswer: Business economics is microeconomic in nature and decision oriented. It is normative as it prescribes what the firm should do and uses tools like demand cost and profit analysis to guide managerial decisions.
explanation: Cover its micro basis decision focus normative character and use of economic tools.

text: The law of demand states that other things remaining equal the quantity demanded of a good
subject: Business Economics I
options: Falls when price rises|Rises when price rises|Is unaffected by price|Rises when income falls
explanation: Demand varies inversely with price under the law of demand.

text: If a ten percent fall in price raises quantity demanded by twenty percent demand is
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Percentage change in quantity exceeds the percentage change in price so demand is elastic.

text: Goods whose demand falls when income rises are called
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Inferior goods are replaced by better substitutes as income rises.

text: A movement along the demand curve is caused by a change in price while a shift is caused by other factors
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Own price causes movement along the curve; income tastes and related prices shift it.

text: Distinguish between a shift and a movement along the demand curve
subject: Business Economics I
correctAnswer: A change in own price moves along the same demand curve. A change in income tastes or related prices shifts the whole curve to a new position.
explanation: Movement is a quantity response to price; a shift is a change in demand itself.

text: Explain the determinants of price elasticity of demand
subject: Business Economics I
correctAnswer: Elasticity depends on availability of substitutes the proportion of income spent the nature of the good and time period. More substitutes and higher budget share make demand more elastic.
explanation: Cover substitutes income share necessity versus luxury and time.

text: When price falls from 20 to 16 and quantity demanded rises from 40 to 48 units the price elasticity of demand is
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Percentage change in quantity is 8 over 40 or twenty percent and in price is 4 over 20 or twenty percent so elasticity equals one.

text: The law of diminishing marginal utility explains why the demand curve slopes
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: As marginal utility falls with each extra unit the consumer pays less so the curve slopes down.

text: Total utility is maximum when marginal utility becomes
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Total utility peaks when marginal utility reaches zero; beyond that it becomes negative.

text: An indifference curve shows combinations of two goods giving equal satisfaction to the consumer
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: All points on an indifference curve yield the same level of total utility.

text: State the law of equi-marginal utility
subject: Business Economics I
correctAnswer: A consumer maximises satisfaction by spending so that the marginal utility per rupee is equal across all goods consumed.
explanation: Equilibrium requires the last rupee spent on every good to yield equal marginal utility.

text: Describe the properties of indifference curves
subject: Business Economics I
correctAnswer: Indifference curves slope downward are convex to the origin and never intersect each other. Higher curves represent higher utility levels.
explanation: Cover the negative slope convexity and non intersection properties.

text: In the short run when one factor is fixed and others vary the firm is operating under the law of
subject: Business Economics I
options: Variable proportions|Constant proportions|Diminishing returns to scale|Increasing returns to scale
explanation: The law of variable proportions applies when one input is fixed and others vary.

text: Costs that do not change with the level of output are called
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Fixed costs remain constant in the short run regardless of output.

text: When marginal product is at its maximum the marginal cost is at its minimum
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Marginal cost and marginal product are inversely related.

text: Define fixed cost and variable cost with one example each
subject: Business Economics I
correctAnswer: Fixed costs such as rent do not vary with output. Variable costs such as raw materials vary directly with output.
explanation: The distinction holds only in the short run.

text: Explain the law of variable proportions and its three stages
subject: Business Economics I
correctAnswer: The law shows output change as more units of a variable factor combine with a fixed factor. It has increasing then diminishing then negative returns stages. Production is rational only in stage two.
explanation: Describe each stage and identify the rational stage for production.

text: Total fixed cost is 5000 and total variable cost at ten units is 3000. The total cost is
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Total cost equals fixed cost plus variable cost so 5000 plus 3000 equals 8000.

text: A market with many sellers selling differentiated products is called
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Monopolistic competition has many firms each selling a slightly differentiated product.

text: A market with a single seller and no close substitutes is a
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: A monopoly is a single seller with barriers to entry and no close substitutes.

text: In perfect competition the firm is a price taker
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: With many small firms none can influence the market price.

text: List the features of perfect competition
subject: Business Economics I
correctAnswer: Large number of buyers and sellers homogeneous product free entry and exit and perfect knowledge.
explanation: These features make each firm a price taker.

text: Explain how price and output are determined under monopoly
subject: Business Economics I
correctAnswer: A monopolist faces the whole market demand and maximises profit where marginal revenue equals marginal cost. It sets a price on the demand curve above marginal cost so output is lower and price higher than competition.
explanation: Cover the MR equals MC rule and the resulting higher price and restricted output.

text: Assertion: A monopolist can earn abnormal profits in the long run. Reason: Barriers to entry prevent new firms from entering the market
subject: Business Economics I
options: Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion|Both are true but reason does not explain assertion|Assertion is true but reason is false|Assertion is false but reason is true
explanation: Barriers to entry protect the monopolist from competition allowing persistent abnormal profit.

text: The payment made for the use of land is called
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Rent is the reward to land wages to labour interest to capital and profit to the entrepreneur.

text: The reward paid to the entrepreneur for bearing risk and uncertainty is
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Profit rewards the entrepreneur for organisation and risk bearing.

text: According to Ricardian theory rent arises due to the differing fertility of land
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Ricardo attributed rent to the superior productivity of better land over the marginal land.

text: Define wages and explain the difference between nominal and real wages
subject: Business Economics I
correctAnswer: Wages are the payment to labour. Nominal wages are money paid while real wages are the goods and services that money wages can buy.
explanation: Real wages adjust nominal wages for the price level.

text: Explain the marginal productivity theory of distribution
subject: Business Economics I
correctAnswer: Under perfect competition each factor is paid the value of its marginal product. A firm employs a factor until its marginal revenue product equals its price so every factor is rewarded according to its contribution.
explanation: Cover the MRP equals factor price condition and its assumptions.

text: If the market demand curve for a firm is horizontal the firm operates under
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: A perfectly elastic horizontal demand curve means the firm cannot change the market price.

text: Two firms control an entire market between them. This market structure is a
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: A duopoly is a special case of oligopoly with only two firms.

text: Match the term to its definition
subject: Business Economics I
options: Oligopoly - few interdependent firms|Monopoly - many price takers|Perfect competition - single seller|Monopolistic competition - no product differentiation
explanation: Oligopoly is few interdependent firms while monopoly is a single seller.

text: A good for which demand rises as its price rises is called a
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Giffen goods have a positive price-demand relationship because their income effect outweighs substitution.

text: Read the case: A bakery finds that raising the price of cakes reduces its total revenue while raising the price of bread raises total revenue. Compare the elasticity of demand for the two products
subject: Business Economics I
correctAnswer: Demand for cakes is elastic because a price rise lowers total revenue as quantity falls sharply. Demand for bread is inelastic because a price rise raises total revenue as quantity falls only slightly.
explanation: Relate the total revenue test to the elasticity of each product.

text: Read the case: A firm produces 100 units at an average cost of 50 and a market price of 80. Calculate total revenue total cost and profit per unit
subject: Business Economics I
correctAnswer: Total revenue is 100 times 80 which equals 8000. Total cost is 100 times 50 which equals 5000. Profit is 3000 and profit per unit is 30.
explanation: Profit equals total revenue minus total cost.

text: The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in income is called
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Income elasticity measures how demand responds to changes in consumer income.

text: Cross elasticity of demand between complementary goods is positive
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Complements have negative cross elasticity while substitutes have positive cross elasticity.

text: The output where marginal cost equals marginal revenue is called the
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: A firm maximises profit by producing where marginal cost equals marginal revenue.

text: When average cost falls as output rises the firm enjoys economies of
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Economies of scale reduce long run average cost as output expands.

text: A consumer buys 30 units of a good at a price of 10 per unit. Total expenditure is
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Total expenditure equals price times quantity so 10 times 30 equals 300.

text: The demand curve of a monopolist is the market demand curve itself
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: A monopolist is the only seller so it faces the entire downward sloping market demand.

text: State the assumptions of the law of demand
subject: Business Economics I
correctAnswer: Income tastes and prices of related goods remain constant and there is no expectation of future price change.
explanation: These ceteris paribus assumptions keep the law of demand valid.

text: Explain the concept of production function
subject: Business Economics I
correctAnswer: A production function shows the maximum output obtainable from given quantities of inputs with a given technology. It relates inputs to output and underlies the analysis of returns and costs.
explanation: Cover the input output relationship and the role of technology.

text: Total utility from consuming units is 0 20 35 45 50 50 45 for seven successive units. Marginal utility of the fourth unit is
subject: Business Economics I
explanation: Marginal utility of the fourth unit is total utility of four units minus that of three units so 45 minus 35 equals 10.
